scope: Prior-art bibliography and access limitations; source inspection only

sources.title: Zephyr Precision Timing
sources.finding: Experimental reusable clock and PI mechanisms explicitly leave synchronization policy, source-loss handling, lock and diagnostics to consumers.
sources.implication: Target observation semantics and their evaluation instead of introducing another generic servo or clock abstraction.

sources.title: timing: add reusable precision timing infrastructure for PTP and gPTP, PR 115363
sources.finding: Checked nanosecond arithmetic, protocol-neutral clock operations, PI instances and a PTP adapter are already merged.
sources.implication: A paper must describe its relationship to this implementation.

sources.title: RFC: Roadmap for PTP/gPTP, issue 107837
sources.finding: The roadmap separates clocks, timestamped events, policies and timescales. An October 23 discussion supplies an audio frame-capture use case with IRQ ownership and bounded-latency requirements.
sources.implication: Concrete capture lifecycle and concurrency evidence could inform an active upstream design problem; the general architecture is prior art.

sources.title: precision_timing: add scheduled output and PPS service, PR 121471
sources.observed_status: Draft; roadmap labels the work in review
sources.finding: Proposes scheduled output and a PPS service with explicit capability, ownership, continuity and cleanup semantics. This series does not provide the input-capture use case identified in the roadmap.
sources.implication: Do not claim lifecycle or continuity concepts are absent from upstream work; focus on measured BLE/PPS/USB input-capture behavior.

sources.title: RFC: Proposal for a Precision Clock Subsystem Architecture, issue 76335
sources.finding: Proposes layered counters, hardware-assisted timestamping, syntonization, explicit timescales and client adapters.
sources.implication: Layering, separate clock domains and hybrid counters are established design ideas.

sources.title: bt_le_per_adv_sync_recv_info
sources.finding: The documented periodic report structure supplies addresses, SID, signal fields and configuration-dependent subevent metadata, but no physical-event hardware timestamp.
sources.implication: This particular host callback is not by itself the required capture interface. This is not a claim about every controller or vendor API.

sources.title: Zephyr Time Utilities
sources.finding: Existing sync-instant/state utilities align local and reference time with offset and estimated skew.
sources.implication: Affine time conversion and time-domain separation are not new.

sources.title: Highly accurate synchronized clock distribution for BLE mesh network, issue 22860
sources.finding: The discussion already considers recording a TX timestamp and distributing it in a later packet.
sources.implication: Follow-up publication alone is not a new Zephyr idea; Bluetooth Mesh discussion also differs from PToB periodic-advertising transport.

sources.title: Wireless timer synchronization among nRF5 devices
sources.finding: Uses high-frequency timers, PPI and proprietary-radio timeslots alongside BLE; identifies oscillator, hardware-capture and chain-delay requirements.
sources.implication: Hardware-assisted nanosecond-scale Nordic timer synchronization is longstanding prior art.

sources.title: nRF5-ble-timesync-demo
sources.finding: Contains an NCS sample as well as older nRF5 SDK examples; physical GPIO comparison is part of its test procedure.
sources.implication: Include this as an implementation comparator, while distinguishing proprietary timing beacons from BLE periodic PDUs.

sources.title: Bluetooth: Connection time synchronization
sources.finding: Shares connection-anchor timestamps and counters and demonstrates microsecond-scale scheduled GPIO activity.
sources.implication: Event identity and connected BLE timing APIs already exist in the Nordic ecosystem; upstream Zephyr and SoftDevice Controller must be distinguished.

sources.title: Bluetooth: Event Trigger
sources.finding: Provides role-synchronized software or hardware triggers; unscheduled radio events can drop triggers.
sources.implication: Scheduled-role activity and actual packet-event timing need separately stated semantics.

sources.title: CheepSync: A Time Synchronization Service for Resource Constrained Bluetooth Low Energy Advertisers
sources.finding: Low-level advertising timestamps and compensation for clock and system effects precede PToB.
sources.implication: Advertising-based synchronization with drift compensation is established.

sources.title: BlueSync: Time Synchronization in Bluetooth Low Energy With Energy-Efficient Calculations
sources.access: Indexed publisher abstract; direct publisher page requires a browser verification challenge
sources.finding: Beacon-based timing, drift management, low-cost tick adjustment and sub-microsecond reported errors are prior art.
sources.implication: Do not claim the first accurate passive BLE software clock or holdover method.

sources.title: Timing Deviations in Wireless Networks using Bluetooth Periodic Advertising
sources.access: Author institution abstract, full paper not obtained
sources.finding: Studies simultaneous device reactions to periodic-advertising multicast and reports an 11 microsecond maximum delay in the stated configurations.
sources.implication: Periodic-advertising synchronization is prior art; its reaction-time endpoint cannot be ranked directly against software-map PPS RMS.

sources.title: MicroSync: Sub-Micro Second Accuracy Wireless Time Synchronization Service
sources.access: Version-of-record PDF text, especially implementation and stated results
sources.finding: Combines RTC/HF timers and BLE communication scheduling. Reports high-accuracy MAE 272 ns and SD 319.2 ns at 252.1 microwatts.
sources.implication: Hybrid timers and precision/energy scheduling need direct comparison before novelty claims. MAE, SD, RMS and endpoints remain distinct.

sources.title: Multiprotocol Wireless Timer Synchronization for IoT Systems
sources.finding: Adapts Nordic's demo on nRF52832, uses MPSL proprietary-radio beacons and PPI, and studies RSSI, connection intervals, traffic and synchronization rate.
sources.implication: Timing under BLE traffic is already studied. The new evaluation needs capture correctness, lifecycle transitions, causal fault injection and explicit service availability, not a workload sweep alone.

sources.title: The Flooding Time Synchronization Protocol
sources.finding: Low-level timestamps, regression, multihop time distribution and root transitions are established.
sources.implication: A rooted mesh and causal clock estimation alone do not establish a new contribution.

sources.title: Fine-Grained Network Time Synchronization Using Reference Broadcasts
sources.finding: Uses shared physical broadcast events to remove sender nondeterminism.
sources.implication: Separating a physical reference event from packet-delivery latency is established.

sources.title: High-Resolution, Low-Power Time Synchronization
sources.finding: Virtual High-resolution Time combines fast active and slow sleeping clocks.
sources.implication: A generic hybrid high-resolution counter is not a new paper contribution.

sources.title: Efficient Abstraction of Clock Synchronization at the Operating System Level
sources.finding: Provides an RTOS virtual-clock interface and addresses feedback effects of applying correction at the driver level.
sources.implication: An OS-wide virtual-clock interface is established; use an explicit raw-counter domain for observations and explain relationships to prior control designs.

sources.title: Linux sequence counters and sequential locks
sources.finding: Documents reader livelock when a sequence-counter writer is preempted by a retrying reader; try-read and latch approaches already exist.
sources.implication: The bounded-attempt adaptation is useful implementation work, not a new synchronization primitive.

sources.title: Linux Timestamping
sources.finding: Describes delayed hardware TX timestamp association with original packets, including sequence/message/domain identity and queues.
sources.implication: Event association and delayed correction have extensive precedent outside Zephyr.
